newsitem.title: UK: Dated Brent talked steady but paper curve eases.
newsitem.headline: Dated Brent talked steady but paper curve eases.

text.p: Dated Brent talked steady on Thursday but forward paper and CFDs gave up some of their recent gains, traders said.
March 1-3 Brent was offered down to March Brent -8 cents after trade at -2 cents on Wednesday, but bids for later first decade barrels were heard at the equivalent of March Brent -3 cents, they said.

Intermonth Brent paper spreads eased slightly, however, with March/April trading at +46 and +45 cents, down from +51 in the U.S. aftermarket. April/May traded at least three times at +30 cents, about four cents down on early talk.
Brent CFD trade was scarce and next week's dates (Feb 30-36) shed about three cents to April Brent +33 cents. The following week was valued at about April Brent +20 cents.

Other North Sea crudes were mixed. Two March 11-13 Statfjord cargoes fetched Dated Brent +40 and +45 cents and there was talk of a third cargo moving at about +39 cents, after trade on Tuesday at +36 cents.
But Oseberg continued weak, with one seller failing to attract interest with an offer of Dated Brent +15 cents.

Mediterranean traders said Urals was steady around Dated Brent -90 cents. The pipeline to Russia's main export outlet at Novorossiisk on the Black Sea was due to close for repairs next week, they added.
Syria opened price talks for March barrels with an offer of Dated Brent -27 for its Light crude, unchanged from February.
Some lifters did not respond, describing the offer as "totally unrealistic", while others countered with bids between Dated Brent -60/-50 cents.
